newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up, awaiting cabinet on IMF.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up, awaiting cabinet on IMF.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to rise marginally as investors waited for a cabinet announcement scheduled later on Tuesday on an economic rescue plan from the IMF, brokers said.

"The cabinet decision on the IMF assistance will help boost the market sentiment. I think there will be some profit-taking as investors believe that some financial institutions would be affected at least in short-term after the adoption of IMF measures," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index closed 11.78 points higher at 663.82 on 3.4 billion baht turnover on Monday.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Monday he would seek cabinet approval of the framework of the IMF-backed package on Tuesday.
Central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said clearer details of the package would likely emerge by early next week.

The Japanese newspaper Yomiuri Shimbun reported on Tuesday the IMF, the Asian Development Bank, Japan's Export-Import Bank and Japanese commercial banks would provide a total of $10 billion to support Thailand's economy. The report was not confirmed by Thai officials. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642, email: bangkok.newsroom@reuters.com
